chapter: New York bands and the first records
title: Waiting for a New York union card; society band work
summary: Barred from the Biltmore job by union rules, he freelances with Meyer Davis and Lanin, as all the stars did.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Well listen, Red, we musn't get too much off the track now, from -- away from the development of your career. So I think maybe we ought to get straight back onto that. You --
Where was I?
Well you and Mildred married and -- left Paul --
Oh, well we came to New York they went to the Biltmore, and I couldn't go. I didn't have a New York card.
OH, I see.
So I had to leave, so at that time you had to --
Sweat it out for six months?
Year. Not Six months like right now. Had to take a year, they were trying to keep people out. Everyone wanted to come to New York then.
Yeah.
So I jobbed around, I went with Meyer Davis, and I worked with the Lanin Lannen boys --
Oh, you did?
Yeah, oh yeah. Well everybody did in those early days. Tommy Dorsey, Jimmy Dorsey --
Yeah, that's where the work was --
-- Benny Goodman, Artie Shaw --
Sure.
-- everybody worked with them --
Cause that's where the work was.
I remember going -- Bunny Berigan -- we used to go out and work on Long Island and remember those garden parties in the summertime?
Yeah.
And in one part of the forest would be Lanin Lannen and another part Meyer Davis.
Funny.
